SMTO-CFG-0005 — The Gateway's command time limit can't be negative

GUID: ecffd9dc-46e2-445c-983f-87320f4ccde3
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-exec-timeout-seconds-must-be-zero
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) was given a negative time limit for commands, so it stopped before starting. Nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, find where GATEWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is set, such as the script or service that starts it, and change it to 0 or a positive number. The value is how many seconds one command may run, and a negative amount of time isn't possible. If you can't find it, ask the person who set up that computer.
  2. Use 0 if commands should have no time limit, which is the normal default. Zero turns this limit off; you can still stop a task yourself at any time.
  3. Start the Gateway again, then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection. This confirms the Gateway started and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway starts, and Settings › Setup › Gateways shows it as Connected.

If it still fails

  • Send the Gateway's startup message to the person who installed the Gateway. Don't set a very small limit just to get past this; commands that need longer would be stopped partway.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Settings validation rejected GATEWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (exec_timeout_seconds) because it is negative; zero is accepted and disables the execution timeout.

What this means

  • Gateway settings validation finds exec_timeout_seconds negative; zero is accepted to disable the configured execution timeout. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway settings validation finds exec_timeout_seconds negative; zero is accepted to disable the configured execution timeout.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and distinguish execution timeout from terminal-idle and model timeouts.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (or exec_timeout_seconds in the Gateway instance's configuration/managed.json) to 0 or a positive number of seconds and restart the Gateway. This is the per-command execution timeout, separate from the terminal-idle and model timeouts.
  • Set GATEWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to a nonnegative duration; choose zero only if disabling this timeout is intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Gateway startup accepts the intended nonnegative execution timeout.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
